submitter: site_delivery_and_editor lane, fixing bugs_open/466 — the approve-to-apply path, met for the first time on the first paid site (boxingonline, 2026-09-03).
rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 (d04c1bc1) returned REVISE on one high-severity gating objection plus four mediums. I have acted on every one rather than defending any, and two of them found real gaps.

THE GATING OBJECTION WAS RIGHT (bug_historian): a fan-out that proceeds on an EMPTY array files zero items while the review row still reads `complete` — the same silent completion this whole change exists to fix, one level down. The code already reported it via `fan_out_note`; what it did NOT have was a TEST, and an unasserted behaviour is one refactor from gone. Now pinned: no INSERT is even expected, `follow_on_item_ids` must be a present-and-empty `[]` (an absent key reads as success), and the note must name the empty array. Mutation-killed.

THE GUARDIAN WAS RIGHT TOO, and this is the more valuable of the two. My dead-address guard checked EXISTENCE only. The other half is worse: a target that still exists but MOVED since the proposal was written. `field_updates` is a full-field replacement frozen at proposal time, so applying a stale one reverts everything changed since, and on a single-field component that is the whole component (LANDMINES 2026-08-17). One query now answers both — `SELECT pc.updated_at > $3` — where no row means gone and true means moved, each with its own reason text handed back to the approver. [MEASURED 2026-09-03] 0 of the 31 parked edits are stale today, so this arm costs nothing now, which is exactly when to add it rather than after it costs something. Mutation-killed.

THREE CLAIMS THE ROUND SAID I ASSERTED RATHER THAN MEASURED. All three are now measured and the measurements are recorded IN THE HANDLER, not just here, because each is the kind of claim that goes stale by ADDITION and reads as current for ever:
  * BLAST RADIUS (guardian + prior_art_librarian, medium). They were right that a single grep is not a search. The live scan is stronger than what I claimed: across EVERY live, non-snapshot, undeleted agent_definition, exactly ONE workflow step configures on_approve — copy-editor's `request_review`. Not 'one other consumer'; ZERO others. fork_theme_from_site_action.go writes an on_approve from Go with no item_type, no include_fields and no checkpoint:true, so HandleApproveWorkItem 400s it before this code. The query is in the comment so the next reader re-runs it rather than re-arguing it.
  * DEDUP (guidelines, medium — and this one could have been fatal). idx_swi_dedup is UNIQUE(site_id, item_key) WHERE item_key IS NOT NULL AND status NOT IN (the terminal set). This handler has never set item_key, so every child is NULL and the partial index excludes it: N children cannot collide. Deliberately left that way — minting a per-element key would convert a cannot-happen into a can-fail-at-insert, and the endpoint already refuses a second press because the review row is no longer needs_human_review. I also read both BEFORE-INSERT triggers on the table: refuse_untraceable_park returns immediately for status <> 'deferred', and these rows are 'triaged'.
  * PRIOR ART (prior_art_librarian, medium). Checked: there is no generic one-item-fans-into-N helper on the admin side. `create_work_item` is a workflow ACTION reachable by an agent step, not by an HTTP handler. And `createFollowOn` is the SINGLE creation path — the fan-out calls the same closure the single-item branch calls, N times, rather than forking a second inserter (answering reuse_agent).

THE ARCHITECTURE SEAT'S LINE IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THE ROUND and is now recorded in the handler: a SECOND live consumer of fan_out_from reopens the RFC_022 question and should come back as needs_rfc, not as another same-commit wiring. That is exactly the accumulation RFC_022 exists to catch, and it would otherwise have had to be re-derived by whoever wires the second one.

DEBUG_HISTORIAN's TOCTOU point (medium) is stated rather than engineered around: the check and the INSERT are not one transaction, the window is milliseconds, and its outcome is today's behaviour (the item dies at load_edit_context), not a new failure. Saying so in the comment is the honest version; wrapping a transaction around it would buy nothing measurable.

EDITQUALITY's three objections were sketch-fidelity, and the sketches below are corrected: resolveIncluded now binds fieldName, the fan-out sketch shows where `elements` comes from, and edit 4 shows follow_on_item_ids being written rather than implying it inside an opaque jsonb merge.

Unchanged from round 1 and still the argument for shipping: [MEASURED 2026-09-03, all history] 42 include_fields mentions across 21 items since 2026-08-24, ZERO ever resolvable; 16 review items parked in needs_human_review carrying 31 edits that nobody can currently approve.

plan.summary: Repair `include_fields` (fall back to the approved body when the review spec cannot hold the name — which, measured, is always), and add two opt-in keys to `on_approve`: `fan_out_from` (file one follow-on per element of a named array in the approved data, merging that element's fields at the top of the child spec) and `defaults` (fields the proposal does not carry). Refuse and REPORT a fanned-out element whose page_component_id no longer exists, rather than filing an item guaranteed to die. Record what the approval actually produced on the review row, so `complete` stops being the only thing the approver sees.

edits.rationale: include_fields consults `spec` FIRST (documented semantics preserved exactly — nothing that resolves today can change) and the admin's submitted body second. A name absent from both is now ABSENT from the child spec rather than written as an explicit null; the observed damage was `copy_edit: null, page_target: null`, a shape that reads as real, empty content.

One follow-on per element. Merge order is defaults, then include_fields, then the element's own fields, then the provenance fields LAST — so an element carrying its own `approved_by` or `source_item_id` cannot overwrite who approved it. Children do not duplicate the whole approved payload; `source_item_id` points at the review row, which holds it. ROUND 2: createFollowOn is the SINGLE creation path — the fan-out calls the same closure the single-item branch calls, N times, not a second inserter (reuse_agent). [MEASURED 2026-09-03] idx_swi_dedup excludes NULL item_key, which this handler has never set, so N children cannot collide; a per-element key is deliberately NOT minted because it would turn a cannot-happen into a can-fail-at-insert (guidelines). An EMPTY or wrong-typed array is the gating case and is now pinned by a test: nothing filed, and fan_out_note says why.

ROUND 2, answering the guardian: existence-only was the weaker half. The address rots TWO ways — DELETED (a rerender replaces the row with a new id; [MEASURED 2026-09-03] 3 of 31 parked edits) and MOVED (the row survives but its content changed after the proposal was written, so a full-field field_updates replacement reverts everything since — LANDMINES 2026-08-17; [MEASURED 2026-09-03] 0 of 31 today, so the arm costs nothing now). ONE query answers both. Either way: refuse and REPORT with a distinct reason, never file. Scoped to the fan-out path, so no existing consumer changes. TOCTOU is stated, not engineered around: the window is milliseconds and its outcome is today's behaviour.

466 candidate 3. A review row reading `complete` while its spawned work failed is 'a complete work item is not a repaired artefact' aimed at a PERSON. The row's result now carries follow_on_items[], skipped_edits[] and fan_out_note; `follow_on_item` is kept for existing readers and names the first. follow_on_item_ids is ALWAYS present in the response, so 'nothing was filed' is a visible [] rather than an absent key that reads as success.

Five tests, and all four load-bearing arms were MUTATION-TESTED rather than merely observed green: removing the dead-address guard, removing the approved-body fallback, making fan-out the default, and dropping the element-field merge each kill exactly the test that names them. The test asserting the opt-in default is the one that matters most to a reviewer — it is what stops a later tidy-up making fan-out unconditional for every checkpoint consumer. ROUND 2 adds two: the MOVED-target refusal, and the gating case — an empty fan_out array must file nothing AND say so. Six mutations now, all killed: the four originals plus (5) neutering the staleness arm and (6) dropping the empty-array note.

The config half. Replaces the two names that can never resolve with `domain` (a key the review spec genuinely holds, and what the two proven hand-filed items carried), adds fan_out_from='edits' and defaults={edit_type:'content_edit'}. [MEASURED 2026-09-03] of the 41 proposed edits across those 21 items, 41 carry page_component_id, ZERO carry edit_type, ZERO carry page_name — so edit_type must be defaulted and page_name must NOT be, because every edit is addressed by page_component_id and a defaulted page_name would be a guess applied to every page. Snapshot table, anchor guard that aborts if the step has drifted or fan_out_from is already present, and a DO/RAISE verify (a verify block of bare SELECTs cannot stop the COMMIT). ROUND 2 (guardian): filed as config_change, not add — the SQL file is the vehicle, but the SURFACE being changed is copy-editor's request_review step config in agent_definitions.default_config. The anchor guard's exact predicate: it aborts unless exactly one live copy-editor row exists, on_approve is present at workflow.steps.request_review.config, its item_type is section_edit and handler_agent is section-editor, and fan_out_from is NOT already present.

It is unaffected, and it is the whole of the rest of the population.
